localizedValues.name: Viewpoint Beach
localizedValues.description: A 4.5 km hike on the West Canyon Trail leads to Viewpoint Beach Campground. For current trail conditions, please refer to the trail report on the Golden Ears Provincial Park website. The campground has 20 campsites. The maximum people per campsite is four (4). There is a maximum of three (3) campsites per reservation. The maximum tents per campsite is two (2), for example one 4-person tent or two 2-person tents, and all tents must fit within the campsite. The campground has one outhouse and one bear cache for food storage. Boil or treat all water. Mountain bikes are not permitted on this trail. Fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Golden Ears Park backcountry areas. All garbage must be packed out.

localizedValues.name: Hiker's Beach
localizedValues.description: A 5.3 km hike on the West Canyon Trail leads to Hiker’s Beach Campground, located across Gold Creek from Viewpoint Beach. The campground has 20 campsites. The maximum people per campsite is four (4). There is a maximum of three (3) campsites per reservation. The maximum tents per campsite is two (2), for example one 4-person tent or two 2-person tents, and all tents must fit within the campsite. There is one bear cache for food storage. There are no toilet facilities; a pit toilet may be accessed at Viewpoint Beach across the creek. Boil or treat all water. Mountain bikes are not permitted on this trail. Fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Golden Ears Park backcountry areas. All garbage must be packed out.

localizedValues.name: Alder Flats
localizedValues.description: A 5.7 km hike on the West Canyon Trail leads to Alder Flats Campground, with an elevation gain of approximately 111 m. For current trail conditions, please refer to the trail report on the Golden Ears Provincial Park website. The campground has 10 campsites. The maximum people per campsite is four (4). There is a maximum of three (3) campsites per reservation. The maximum tents per campsite is two (2), for example one 4-person tent or two 2-person tents, and all tents must fit within the campsite. The campground has one outhouse and one bear cache for food storage. Boil or treat all water. Mountain bikes are not permitted on this trail. Fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Golden Ears Park backcountry areas. All garbage must be packed out.

localizedValues.name: Halfmoon Beach
localizedValues.description: A 10 km hike on the East Canyon Trail leads to Halfmoon Beach Campground. For current trail conditions, please refer to the trail report on the Golden Ears Provincial Park website. The campground has 30 campsites. The maximum people per campsite is four (4). There is a maximum of three (3) campsites per reservation. The maximum tents per campsite is two (2), for example one 4-person tent or two 2-person tents, and all tents must fit within the campsite. The campground has one outhouse and one bear cache for food storage. Boil or treat all water. Fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Golden Ears Park backcountry areas. All garbage must be packed out.

localizedValues.name: Panorama Ridge
localizedValues.description: A 10.7 km hike on the Golden Ears Trail leads to Panorama Ridge Campground, with an elevation gain of approximately 1,049 m and a suggested hiking time of seven hours one way. The trail difficulty is strenuous and requires backcountry experience, route finding skills, and navigation equipment. Follow the West Canyon Trail to Alder Flats to reach the Golden Ears Trailhead. For current trail conditions, please refer to the trail report on the Golden Ears Provincial Park website. The campground has 10 campsites: four tent pads and six additional established sleeping areas. The maximum people per campsite is four (4). There is a maximum of three (3) campsites per reservation. The maximum tents per campsite is two (2), for example one 4-person tent or two 2-person tents, and all tents must fit within the campsite. The campground has a urine diversion toilet, an emergency shelter for emergency use only, and a helicopter landing pad that must not be occupied. Boil or treat all water. Mountain bikes are not permitted on this trail. Fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Golden Ears Park backcountry areas. All garbage must be packed out.

localizedValues.name: East Beach
localizedValues.description: 0.5km from the Alouette Lake boat launch on the opposite side of the lake. It is also accessible via walking or cycling on a gated BC Hydro access road. There are 18 numbered campsites. The maximum people per campsite is four (4). There is a maximum of three (3) campsites per reservation. The maximum tents per campsite is two (2), for example one 4-person tent or two 2-person tents, and all tents must fit within the campsite. Making a reservation guarantees your spot but does not assign you a specific campsite. Select your campsite upon arrival to the campground. The campground has 2 pit toilets and 1 bear cache for food storage. Fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in Golden Ears Park backcountry areas. All garbage must be packed out.

localizedValues.name: Backcountry Marine Registration
localizedValues.description: Permit registration allows for overnight camping year-round at Moyer Creek, The Narrows, Alouette River, Raven Creek, Osprey Creek South and North. All other areas of Golden Ears backcountry (including East Beach) require a backcountry reservation.
